themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure collapse
themes_detail.summary: Queens Village is experiencing a cascading infrastructure crisis this week, with curb condition complaints up 900% (15 complaints last week vs. 1.5 weekly average), street signs missing up 586% (6 complaints last week vs. 0.9 average), and uprooted stumps up 500% (3 complaints last week vs. 0.5 average)—suggesting systematic neglect of public right-of-way maintenance that compounds with seasonal weather stress.
evidence: Curb condition complaints: 15 filed last week vs. 1.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 9.55, severity: high)
Street sign missing complaints: 6 filed last week vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.53, severity: high)
Uprooted stump complaints: 3 filed last week vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.0, severity: high)
Community board repeatedly requests street reconstruction funding (recurring budget request), indicating long-term deferred maintenance
reporting_angles: Interview DOT about resource allocation and maintenance scheduling; walk streets with residents documenting hazards
Analyze whether this week's spike correlates with weather events, seasonal budget cycles, or personnel changes

themes_detail.label: Illegal posting epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked 1500% this week (6 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks)—the highest z-score anomaly in the dataset (11.62)—suggesting either coordinated activity, lax enforcement, or a sudden change in community tolerance/awareness.
evidence: Illegal posting complaints: 6 filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 11.62, highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
No sustained spike this week specifically, but 2-week window shows extreme deviation
Community board budget requests include expanded code enforcement, suggesting enforcement capacity is a known problem
reporting_angles: Map where illegal postings are concentrated; interview DSNY/enforcement about staffing and responsiveness
Identify what's being posted (political, commercial, graffiti tags) to understand whether this is organized activity

themes_detail.label: Tree and vegetation overgrowth
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped 329% last week (37 complaints vs. 8.6 weekly average), and litter basket complaints surged 2300% three weeks ago (3 complaints vs. 0.1 average)—indicating Parks Department maintenance backlogs that create safety and sanitation hazards.
evidence: Overgrown tree/branches complaints: 37 filed last week vs. 8.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.41, severity: high)
Litter basket complaints: 3 filed 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69, severity: high)
Community board has made 'better park maintenance' and 'park reconstruction' recurring budget requests, signaling chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Request Parks maintenance schedule for CD 413; document specific locations where overgrowth poses pedestrian hazards
Interview residents about whether vegetation overgrowth has worsened seasonal flooding, visibility at intersections, or pest habitat

themes_detail.label: Residential noise escalation
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints in residential areas rose 67% last week (70 complaints vs. 42 weekly average), a statistically significant spike (z-score: 5.03), potentially driven by seasonal activity, construction, or changes in enforcement response.
evidence: Residential noise complaints: 70 filed last week vs. 42 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.03, severity: high)
Overall noise complaints are already the 7th-highest complaint type in 90-day volume (605 total)
Spike is proportionally smaller than other infrastructure spikes but reflects lived experience of residents
reporting_angles: Determine whether spike correlates with specific events, construction permits filed (630 filed in last 90 days), or seasonal patterns
Interview residents about noise sources (traffic, bars, construction, vehicle modifications) and NYPD response times

themes_detail.label: Off-leash dog complaints surge
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints jumped 471% two weeks ago (5 complaints vs. 0.9 weekly average, z-score: 5.28), a notable spike in a residential neighborhood where pets are common and park safety is a concern.
evidence: Unleashed dog complaints: 5 filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.28, severity: high)
Spike is 2 weeks old, not current this week, but still fresh enough to investigate
No follow-up data showing whether situation has resolved or worsened
reporting_angles: Identify which parks or streets are hotspots; interview residents and Parks enforcement about compliance issues
Determine if spike is tied to seasonal behavior (warm weather, more park use) or an enforcement gap
